column1: # Original WritingDeck plot situations. MIT to the extent copyright subsists; AI-assisted original drafting, not copied modern prompts.
# stable_id|category|genres|premise

wd-p-0202|causality|mystery,realist|A forensic botanist identifies a rare seed in a suspect's coat, then discovers that the seed came from her own laboratory's demonstration kit. The evidence still places the suspect at a relevant meeting, but not at the location on which the prosecution's timetable depends.

wd-p-0203|performance|realist,satire|An understudy learns the lead actor has deliberately taught her an outdated version of a play. On opening night the lead disappears, and the only audience member who recognizes the old ending is the playwright who withdrew permission for the revision.

wd-p-0204|route|speculative,adventure|A courier can shorten any journey by giving away a possession associated with its destination. To carry a medicine home in time, she must surrender the last object connecting her to the person who will need to recognize and admit her.

wd-p-0205|obligation|realist,romance|Two people meet while returning wrongly delivered parcels and begin using the mix-up to see each other. When one parcel contains a notice that would end the other's tenancy, continuing the harmless ritual becomes a decision about withholding urgent information.

wd-p-0206|learning|realist,family|A daughter teaches her father to read using letters from his late wife. He progresses far enough to discover that the daughter has been skipping passages describing choices about her own childhood, and asks her to resume the lesson without explaining them first.

wd-p-0207|causality|speculative,mystery|A physicist can reverse the last minute in a sealed room, but everything brought in during that minute remains outside afterward. Investigating a disappearance requires deciding which apparently impossible absence was caused by the machine and which was staged to resemble it.

wd-p-0208|performance|realist,political|A touring theater company performs in towns that agree to let residents change the final scene. One council submits an ending before the residents can meet, and honoring the booking would turn an exercise in participation into an endorsement of that exclusion.

wd-p-0209|route|realist,adventure|A postal worker finds a sack of undelivered mail at a depot scheduled for closure. Delivering it would demonstrate the need for the route, but several letters would trigger deadlines their recipients could have met only if delivery had occurred years earlier.

wd-p-0210|obligation|speculative,family|An inheritance consists of one wish that can be granted only to a stranger. The heirs agree to find someone deserving, then discover that their repeated tests are manufacturing the hardship they want the wish to solve.

wd-p-0211|learning|mystery,realist|A driving instructor realizes that a nervous pupil already knows the route of an accident she claims never to have witnessed. The pupil learned it from someone else's repeated instructions, and teaching her to drive independently may destroy the pattern that could identify that person.

wd-p-0212|threshold|realist,romance|A couple agrees to move in together when both can afford equal contributions. A pay rise finally makes that possible, but accepting it requires the better-paid partner to supervise the other at work, turning their long-planned equality into a new dependency.

wd-p-0213|classification|speculative,political|A city registers every resident's profession at adulthood and allocates emergency duties accordingly. A flood exposes that the people best able to repair the barriers were classified as unskilled, while changing their status would conscript them away from the families they are protecting.

wd-p-0214|design|realist,mystery|An industrial designer recognizes an obsolete safety feature in a newly patented device. The feature points to a missing prototype, but it also explains why the new device has prevented accidents that the official specification says cannot occur.

wd-p-0215|substitution|realist,family|A son agrees to stand in for his father at a school ceremony, then learns his father has been volunteering there under the son's name. Accepting the thanks would preserve the father's secret effort to repair a past failure while making the son appear responsible for it.

wd-p-0216|proportion|speculative,satire|A town commissions a monument whose size must match the benefactor's actual contribution. The sculptor finds that subtracting the costs imposed on the town would require digging a hole, and the contract specifies that the finished work must remain publicly visible.

wd-p-0217|threshold|mystery,realist|A conservator discovers that a sealed letter will disintegrate if opened in ordinary air. Its owner needs its contents to contest a will, but the only available laboratory belongs to the person whose claim the letter may defeat.

wd-p-0218|classification|realist,political|A council labels buildings temporary to speed emergency repairs. Years later, residents cannot secure permanent services because their homes still carry the designation, and the clerk who can correct it must first prove that the emergency has officially ended.

wd-p-0219|design|speculative,adventure|A habitat designer builds a refuge that admits people according to the hazards they report. A storm drives in travelers who describe an unfamiliar danger, and opening the untested section may expose everyone already sheltered to a threat the design cannot recognize.

wd-p-0220|substitution|realist,romance|A person hired to write a farewell letter falls in love with the recipient's reply. The client wants another letter sent under the same arrangement, and the writer must decide whether continuing the exchange deepens a deception or honors the feelings the client cannot express alone.

wd-p-0221|proportion|realist,family|A family agrees to divide caregiving duties according to the time each relative has available. The spreadsheet shows a fair balance until one caregiver records travel and recovery time, forcing everyone to confront which hours they have treated as someone else's unlimited resource.

wd-p-0222|sequence|mystery,realist|A video editor finds that the raw footage of a celebrated rescue has correct timestamps but an impossible sequence of shadows. The discrepancy points not to a staged rescue, but to a second intervention the credited rescuer has been paid to omit.

wd-p-0223|constraint|speculative,romance|A couple can hear each other's thoughts only while disagreeing. They learn to manufacture small arguments for intimacy, until a genuine agreement about their future leaves them unable to tell whether the new silence is trust or withdrawal.

wd-p-0224|recognition|realist,adventure|A ranger following a missing hiker finds trail markers placed according to an obsolete rescue manual. The hiker is following instructions the ranger herself taught years earlier, and reaching him requires predicting which dangerous advice he will trust next.

wd-p-0225|withdrawal|realist,political|A respected volunteer resigns from a public committee rather than endorse an unfair decision. The committee uses her departure to claim unanimous approval, and challenging the record would require her to return to the institution she meant to stop legitimizing.

wd-p-0226|intention|speculative,mystery|A device records the last deliberate use of any object. A detective tests a suspected weapon and finds an act of care, then discovers that the person who cleaned it understood exactly how the device distinguishes use from preparation.

wd-p-0227|sequence|realist,family|Two sisters discover that their mother's recipe book is arranged by the order in which family relationships broke down. Cooking through it together brings them to a blank page dated to a quarrel neither remembers participating in.

wd-p-0228|constraint|realist,satire|A grant requires an arts organization to demonstrate that its program can operate without ongoing funding. The director designs a convincing unpaid trial, then realizes that success will prove the funder's case for withholding the wages the trial participants need.

wd-p-0229|recognition|speculative,political|A city replaces identity documents with a system that recognizes people through those who know them. A newcomer begins helping an isolated resident, and both become harder to register because neither yet has the recognized connections needed to vouch for the other.

wd-p-0230|withdrawal|mystery,realist|A witness withdraws an accurate statement after learning it will be used to support a broader allegation she knows is false. The investigator must preserve the useful evidence without forcing her to become the apparent source of a claim she rejects.

wd-p-0231|intention|realist,romance|A couple each plans a surprise that requires the other to be away from home on the same evening. Their efforts to protect the surprises produce convincing evidence of avoidance, and the friend coordinating both has promised not to reveal either plan.

wd-p-0232|compression|speculative,adventure|A shuttle can carry everyone stranded on a moon if their luggage is reduced to a single shared trunk. The passengers discover that several seemingly personal objects are components of the navigation system their hosts dismantled to keep them warm.

wd-p-0233|attention|realist,family|A grandfather gives every family member a different small repair to complete before a reunion. They assume he is testing their competence, but combining the tasks reveals a practical adaptation that would let him keep living at home without announcing his declining mobility.

wd-p-0234|threshold|realist,political|A public clinic opens appointments whenever waiting time exceeds a legal limit. Its administrator discovers that the booking system resets the clock whenever a patient accepts a changed date, making the most cooperative patients appear to have waited least.

wd-p-0235|classification|mystery,realist|A librarian finds that every book reported missing from one branch has been shelved correctly under an old classification. The pattern directs her to a collection removed from the public catalog, but restoring it would disclose the readers whose annotations made it identifiable.

wd-p-0236|design|speculative,family|A family installs a door that opens only when the visitor is sincerely welcome. It begins refusing a relative everyone openly invites, and the household must distinguish fear of conflict from a wish to exclude before an approaching storm makes the refusal dangerous.

wd-p-0237|substitution|realist,adventure|A race official discovers that a runner has completed a dangerous course while using another entrant's registration. The substitute was carrying medicine along the only open route, but awarding the finish would erase the original entrant's recorded decision to withdraw.

wd-p-0238|proportion|realist,romance|Two partners agree to exchange handmade gifts costing the same amount. One finds that the other's gift used months of unpaid training, and trying to equalize the price threatens to turn an act of attention into a competition neither intended.

wd-p-0239|sequence|speculative,mystery|A station receives emergency instructions in reverse order, with each message arriving only after the previous step is completed. The engineer finds that the first required action will destroy the instrument needed to verify whether later messages came from a trustworthy source.

wd-p-0240|constraint|realist,family|A parent writes a will requiring the family house to remain unchanged for one year. A disabled heir needs immediate alterations to live there, and the executor discovers that the parent imposed the rule to protect an object rather than the building itself.

wd-p-0241|recognition|realist,political|A town offers compensation only to businesses listed in an old directory. A market organizer can prove that unlisted vendors traded there, but doing so requires customers to acknowledge purchases they once denied in order to protect the vendors from restrictive licensing rules.

wd-p-0242|withdrawal|speculative,romance|Two people use a service that quietly removes reminders of a relationship after separation. One cancels the process halfway through and finds that the other has received memories stripped of the practical commitments they still need to settle together.

wd-p-0243|intention|mystery,family|A woman discovers that her aunt has been sending anonymous complaints about her own building. The complaints are accurate, but their timing suggests that she wants the building repaired before another resident can carry out a long-planned departure.

wd-p-0244|compression|realist,political|A council requires residents to summarize objections in one sentence. A clerk notices that objections from one group are consistently rejected as multiple issues because the policy combines the housing, transport, and care decisions their lives cannot separate.

wd-p-0245|attention|speculative,satire|A city's advertising system must honor each resident's stated interests exactly. A resident lists only public maintenance, causing every neglected repair to appear across commercial screens, and the system's owners offer personal compensation if she changes her preferences.

wd-p-0246|threshold|mystery,realist|A building inspector finds that an alarm sounds only when a supposedly empty room contains two people. Testing it requires a second witness, but everyone with access insists that entering together would violate a condition attached to the building's transfer.

wd-p-0247|classification|realist,family|A woman sorting her late partner's papers finds that the folders marked unfinished contain completed work never sent to its intended recipients. Delivering it would honor the effort while overriding the partner's deliberate decision not to make those relationships into obligations.

wd-p-0248|design|realist,romance|A couple commissions a house with two separate workspaces, then discovers the architect has combined them to satisfy a requirement only one partner mentioned privately. Changing the design requires explaining why the hidden requirement mattered more than the shared plan.

wd-p-0249|substitution|speculative,political|An election permits voters to delegate a ballot to someone they trust. A public-interest group discovers that delegation chains end with one person who never agreed to receive them, and canceling the chains would disenfranchise people who can no longer vote in person.

wd-p-0250|proportion|mystery,realist|A photographer notices that the scale model used to reconstruct an accident includes one oversized object. Correcting its dimensions makes the official explanation impossible, but the model was built by a witness whose apparent exaggeration preserved a detail every measurement team missed.

wd-p-0251|attention|realist,adventure|A harbor pilot notices that a channel buoy has been moved just far enough to divert ships away from a damaged quay. Restoring it would make the chart accurate while directing the arriving relief vessel toward a hazard not yet entered in the official warnings.
